The anthology's issue 180
(https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/issues/180) works through the
owner's reading feed by how often a paper was returned to: papers opened on
three or more separate days, ranked from the papers-feed snapshot of 30
September. Twenty-nine of them were absent from the anthology. This entry
records what that list meant for this record.

**The trap: the ranking checked one record.** The worklist was computed
against the anthology's `arxiv:` ids only, so six papers already held here
looked unfiled: the work capacity of channels with memory ([LIT-041](../../record/literature.d/LIT-041.md)),
collective intelligence ([LIT-046](../../record/literature.d/LIT-046.md)), community detection with Ricci flow
([LIT-004](../../record/literature.d/LIT-004.md)), spectral networks ([LIT-017](../../record/literature.d/LIT-017.md)), sharing disinformation incidents
([LIT-083](../../record/literature.d/LIT-083.md)) and ZipNN ([LIT-268](../../record/literature.d/LIT-268.md)). Any future pass over the feed should
check both records' ids before calling a paper absent.

**Filed here.** Chuai & Zhao's *Anger makes fake news viral online*
([LIT-379](../../record/literature.d/LIT-379.md)) came here at the owner's direction: how emotion drives the
spread of false news is not something an anthology topic holds. It is a

Döring & Isham's *'What is a Thing?': Topos Theory in the Foundations of
Physics* ([LIT-378](../../record/literature.d/LIT-378.md), with [NOTE-326](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-326.md)) was first set aside as out of
scope for both records. The owner corrected that: it is the one-volume
statement of the topos programme whose four papers ([LIT-343](../../record/literature.d/LIT-343.md), [LIT-335](../../record/literature.d/LIT-335.md),
[LIT-299](../../record/literature.d/LIT-299.md), [LIT-310](../../record/literature.d/LIT-310.md)) this record already holds, and it is filed `Active` and
read in full. By the authors' own account it is mostly those four papers
reprinted. It does not settle [THEORY-037](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-037.md), because it again leaves the
Heyting implication unwritten.

**Held in both, under [ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md).** Two works now have an entry on each side,
and each side reads them for a question of its own:

- *On Context-Content Uncertainty Principle* ([LIT-377](../../record/literature.d/LIT-377.md), with
  [NOTE-325](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-325.md)). This record holds the v1 the owner read, a cognitive and
  information-theoretic framework, and rejects it on its proofs: a theorem
  stated backwards, a false KL inequality (q = (.5, .25, .25),
  p = (.8, .1, .1) gives 0.322 bits against the 0.578 the inequality needs),
  and simulations the abstract promises and the paper does not contain. The
  anthology holds the author's v2, a different paper under a new title that
  makes claims about generalization, mixture-of-experts routing and
  alignment, as a seed with no experiments.
- *ZipNN* ([LIT-268](../../record/literature.d/LIT-268.md)). This record reads it for where the redundancy in stored
  weights sits; the anthology files it as a systems paper on checkpoint
  storage and transfer.

The entries name each other once the anthology's codes are permanent: its
side is filed with temporary codes and is renamed when it merges, so the
`ANTH-LIT-…` citations [ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md) asks for are a follow-up.

**Also held in the anthology now.** The work-capacity, collective
intelligence and Ricci-flow papers were first read on the anthology side and
not filed there, because no anthology topic held them honestly. The owner
approved the topics its reader proposed (`agents-and-environments` and

## Xin Li's structural-learning programme, read as one

*2026-10-01 16:48:51 · curation · record*

**What changed and why.** [LIT-373](../../record/literature.d/LIT-373.md) and [LIT-374](../../record/literature.d/LIT-374.md) were first read one at a time, and each was filed `Rejected` largely on
mathematical slips. Those slips included an "if and only if" that should be "if", a pseudo-dimension that should be
fat-shattering, a bouquet built with open covers where partitions were wanted, and a word used in two senses. The owner
objected on two counts. The papers are pieces of one research programme and must be read together, and the slips were
minutiae: what matters is whether the major takeaways are argued well.

One reader then read both papers together. It also read the author's two companion papers, which are filed here:
- [LIT-375](../../record/literature.d/LIT-375.md), arXiv 2602.07974 v2, the fullest formal statement;
- [LIT-376](../../record/literature.d/LIT-376.md), arXiv 2603.15412 v1, "Local Urysohn Width".

It read charitably: a technical error counts only if a major takeaway depends on it and its sensible repair does not
save it.

**The programme.** Structure is discovered by costly search, condensed into frozen context tokens, and then reused
cheaply. Discovering structure and using it are separate problems, with separate complexities (width against VC
dimension) and separate mechanisms (scaffold against flow, router against experts). [LIT-373](../../record/literature.d/LIT-373.md) is the cognitive and
neural statement of it. [LIT-375](../../record/literature.d/LIT-375.md) and [LIT-376](../../record/literature.d/LIT-376.md) are the formal statements, and [LIT-374](../../record/literature.d/LIT-374.md) is the alignment and
architecture statement.

**Verdicts on the takeaways.**
- **Width is incomparable with VC dimension.** Established in repaired form. [LIT-376](../../record/literature.d/LIT-376.md)'s bouquet is the consistent
  construction the others lacked. The moral drawn from it, that "scaling cannot repair structure", is undermined: the
  comparison is with a per-cell smooth predictor class, not with what a model can represent. Width is in effect a
  covering number at scale, and [LIT-376](../../record/literature.d/LIT-376.md)'s own Remark 8.11 concedes that the obstruction is metric, not topological.
- **An error floor below width (the "phase transition").** Established in repaired form, but close to definitional.
- **Width is estimable from data.** The Ω(w log w) discovery cost is established. The spectral estimator is plausible
  but under-argued: it converges to a count relative to a given predictor, not to width.
- **Decouple router training from task loss, and freeze settled contexts.** Plausible but under-argued. It is a
  testable design hypothesis with continual-learning precedent, but the additive bound it is said to follow from holds
  for joint training too.
- **Amortisation: stored search makes inference cheap.** Argued well enough to take seriously, once "Savitch" is read
  as memoisation. The idea is borrowed. The exponential-reach scaling law ([LIT-373](../../record/literature.d/LIT-373.md) Theorem 2) is not argued.
- **Collapse defeats the curse of dimensionality, and equals free-energy minimisation.** Plausible but under-argued,
  because it moves the curse into the cost of learning the collapse. The equivalence with free-energy minimisation is
  asserted.
- **The neural instantiation.** Plausible but under-argued: the predictions do not discriminate it from standard
  consolidation accounts.
- **Alignment is a scaffold property.** Not argued.

**Standings.**
- **[LIT-373](../../record/literature.d/LIT-373.md)** stays `Rejected`, on new grounds. After repair its core restates amortised inference and complementary
  learning systems, its predictions do not discriminate, and its one original quantitative claim is unargued.
- **[LIT-374](../../record/literature.d/LIT-374.md)** goes from `Rejected` to `Proposed`. It is the only place the decoupling and safety material appears, so it
  is not superseded, though its learning theory is better read in [LIT-375](../../record/literature.d/LIT-375.md).
- **[LIT-375](../../record/literature.d/LIT-375.md)** and **[LIT-376](../../record/literature.d/LIT-376.md)** are `Proposed`.
- [NOTE-321](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-321.md) and [NOTE-322](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-322.md) carry new summaries and a superseding "Joint re-reading" section. Their first readings stay in
  place below, as the record of what was said.

What would settle the programme is one set of synthetic benchmarks of known width:
- a sweep of the number of contexts, comparing routed learners with capacity-matched monolithic models;
- recovery of width from a cold start;
- decoupled against joint router training, compared on forgetting and on boundary error.

A THEORY is not yet warranted. The proved results are a covering number and a coupon-collector bound, and the
explanatory claim (that forgetting is router drift, and that decoupling prevents it) has no evidence in the record. A
draft is held for when an empirical source is filed.

**Versions.** Both companion identifiers now serve different papers from the ones read.
- arXiv 2602.07974 v1 is "Beyond Optimization", so the entry is dated by v2.
- arXiv 2603.15412 v2 (2026-09-14) is "The Metric Slingshot", a grid-cell paper. The entry is v1, the paper the owner
  asked for, with a `source-ok` directive. Its NOTE judges v2 separately, and v2 would be `Rejected`: its grid-ratio
  result depends on a free capacity parameter, and its anaesthesia "confirmation" is post hoc.

**Lesson.** Read a programme's papers together, and judge a hypothesis paper by whether its takeaways are argued, not by
whether every statement survives a referee's pen. Both first readings were right about the slips and wrong about what
they implied.

## Antonio Damasio: six works, and a word for emotion

*2026-10-01 21:17:52 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-385 LIT-386 LIT-387 — Deferred, unread for want of a full text; listed here as filed seeds -->

The owner asked for "some Antonio Damasio" in this record. Six works came
in, chosen to cover the line of his thought from memory to consciousness:

| work | filed | read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Damasio 1989, time-locked retroactivation (*Cognition*) | [LIT-385](../../record/literature.d/LIT-385.md) | no: Deferred, abstract only |
| Damasio 1996, the somatic marker hypothesis (*Phil. Trans. B*) | [LIT-384](../../record/literature.d/LIT-384.md), [NOTE-332](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-332.md) | in full |
| Bechara, Damasio, Tranel & Damasio 1997, deciding advantageously (*Science*) | [LIT-383](../../record/literature.d/LIT-383.md), [NOTE-331](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-331.md) | in full |
| Damasio & Carvalho 2013, the nature of feelings (*Nat. Rev. Neurosci.*) | [LIT-388](../../record/literature.d/LIT-388.md), [NOTE-330](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-330.md) | in full |
| Man & Damasio 2019, homeostasis and feeling machines (*Nat. Mach. Intell.*) | [LIT-386](../../record/literature.d/LIT-386.md) | no: Deferred, abstract only |
| Damasio & Damasio 2023, feelings as the source of consciousness (*Neural Comput.*) | [LIT-387](../../record/literature.d/LIT-387.md) | no: Deferred, abstract only |

**Three are unread because no full text could be reached.** The 1989 paper is
behind ScienceDirect with no open copy. Man & Damasio has no arXiv version and
no open copy. The 2023 paper has a free PDF at MIT Press, but its bot
challenge refused every request. Each is a `Deferred` seed whose
`status_note` says what it rests on.

**A word for emotion ([ADR-014](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-014.md)).** Damasio's subject had no tag, so the owner
asked for one and `emotion-and-affect` joined the vocabulary.

**What the readings found.**

- **Bechara et al. 1997 claims more in its abstract than its statistics show.**
  All 10 controls and none of the 6 patients developed anticipatory skin
  conductance responses. But the controls' preference for the good decks
  before any hunch is not significant. The early skin-conductance effect is
  reported only as a group-by-period interaction, with no test of bad decks
  against good. "Before knowing" holds for the stated strategy, not for
  awareness in general. The record does not yet hold Maia & McClelland's 2004
  critique of the awareness timing.
- **The 1996 paper is a hypothesis paper.** Its evidence is summarised from
  other work without statistics. Two corrections are in its NOTE.
- **The 2013 paper's one shown result** is that feeling survives bilateral
  insula damage, from a single patient. The evolutionary account, animal
  feeling and the cellular proposal are asserted.

**Two things checked along the way.**

- **[NOTE-120](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-120.md) does not cite the 2023 *Neural Computation* paper.** Its
  "Damasio & Damasio 2023" is a different commentary, *Sensing is a far cry
  from sentience* (*Animal Sentience* 33(16)), cited through [LIT-193](../../record/literature.d/LIT-193.md). [NOTE-120](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-120.md)
  reports it correctly. That commentary is the natural next filing for the
  plant-sentience thread.
- **Man & Damasio carries `anthology-candidate`.** Its abstract proposes a
  class of machines without building or measuring one. The anthology's
  `agents-and-environments` topic could hold it, so under [ADR-001](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-001.md) it may be
  theirs. Whether to transfer it is for whoever reads the paper.

## Minsky's Society of Mind and Hofstadter's analogy programme

*2026-10-01 22:26:33 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-429 LIT-418 LIT-416 LIT-435 LIT-417 LIT-437 LIT-428 LIT-423 LIT-420 — Deferred, no lawful full text reached; listed here as filed seeds -->

The owner asked for Marvin Minsky's Society of Mind programme and for Douglas
Hofstadter. Sixteen works came in, eight from each.

## Minsky

| work | filed | read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "A Framework for Representing Knowledge", AI Memo 306 (1974) | [LIT-410](../../record/literature.d/LIT-410.md), [NOTE-337](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-337.md) | in full, OCR of the DSpace scan |
| "Plain Talk About Neurodevelopmental Epistemology", AI Memo 430 (1977) | [LIT-399](../../record/literature.d/LIT-399.md), [NOTE-344](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-344.md) | in full, IJCAI-77 text |
| "K-Lines: A Theory of Memory", AI Memo 516 (1979) / *Cognitive Science* (1980) | [LIT-402](../../record/literature.d/LIT-402.md), [NOTE-352](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-352.md) | in full, the memo |
| "Jokes and the Logic of the Cognitive Unconscious", AI Memo 603 (1980) | [LIT-408](../../record/literature.d/LIT-408.md), [NOTE-361](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-361.md) | in full, the memo |
| *The Society of Mind* (1986) | [LIT-429](../../record/literature.d/LIT-429.md) | no: Deferred |
| "Society of mind: a response to four reviews" (1991) | [LIT-418](../../record/literature.d/LIT-418.md) | no: Deferred, closed |
| *The Emotion Machine* (2006) | [LIT-432](../../record/literature.d/LIT-432.md), [NOTE-348](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-348.md) | in full, the author's posted 2005 draft |
| Singh, "Examining the Society of Mind" (2003) | [LIT-444](../../record/literature.d/LIT-444.md), [NOTE-339](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-339.md) | in full |

The memos form a line by their own account. "Plain Talk" calls itself in part
a sequel to the frames memo, and K-lines complements "Plain Talk". The
filings declare that line as `extends:`, and *The Emotion Machine* extends
*The Society of Mind*.

- **"Plain Talk" does not claim to be first.** It presents the theory, then
  called "The Society of Minds", as unpublished work in progress with Papert.
  K-lines credits one principle to their 1974 lectures, which were not seen.
  Priority is left open.
- **The jokes memo is titled "Jokes and the Logic of the Cognitive
  Unconscious".** The Freud-like title in circulation is wrong.
- ***The Emotion Machine* disagrees with Damasio** ([LIT-383](../../record/literature.d/LIT-383.md) to [LIT-388](../../record/literature.d/LIT-388.md)).
  - The draft treats the body as one more resource. It takes "the opposite
    view" to the bodily account.
  - It reverses the causal direction for Damasio's patient Elliot, without
    evidence.
  - It makes feelings depend on self-models, where Damasio has feelings
    ground consciousness.
  - The two agree only that emotion-free reasoning is a myth.

- **[NOTE-136](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-136.md)'s "argues nearly the opposite" is not yet supported.** As
  [NOTE-136](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-136.md) itself reports, Hofstadter's essay gives a criterion (a Turing
  test of consistent understanding suffices) and a forecast (conscious AI
  "perhaps even by 2033"). Neither says present systems are conscious. He
  plainly dissents from the editors' framing, but "opposite" needs the essay
  read. [NOTE-136](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-136.md) is left unchanged until it is.
- ***Fluid Concepts* reprints the 1992 critique as its chapter 4**, and its
  chapters 5–6 are on Copycat.

## Possible topic words, not added

Two readers proposed words, and neither was needed: `cognition` holds every
work. They are recorded here for when a second line of work wants them:

- `knowledge-representation`: frames, scripts, semantic networks and default
  reasoning, read outside machine learning.
- `cognitive-architecture`: designs for a whole mind, natural or artificial.

## Bridging the society of mind to a conscious United States

*2026-10-02 00:21:43 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-396 LIT-419 LIT-391 LIT-426 — Deferred; listed here as filed seeds -->

The owner asked for a bridge between Minsky's society of mind ([LIT-429](../../record/literature.d/LIT-429.md)
and the memos) and Schwitzgebel's "If materialism is true, the United States
is probably conscious" ([LIT-159](../../record/literature.d/LIT-159.md), [NOTE-131](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-131.md)). Schwitzgebel was already held.
Eleven works came in to fill the seam between them, and one THEORY,
[THEORY-043](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md), states the bridge.

| work | filed | read | where it sits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Selfridge, "Pandemonium" (1959) | [LIT-427](../../record/literature.d/LIT-427.md), [NOTE-360](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-360.md) | in full | decomposition, before Minsky |
| Putnam, "Psychological Predicates" (1967) | [LIT-396](../../record/literature.d/LIT-396.md), [NOTE-335](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-335.md) | skim (excerpt) | the anti-nesting stipulation |
| Block, "Troubles with Functionalism" (1978) | [LIT-407](../../record/literature.d/LIT-407.md), [NOTE-366](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-366.md) | in full | the China brain; first critic of anti-nesting |
| Lycan, "Form, Function, and Feel" (1981) | [LIT-419](../../record/literature.d/LIT-419.md) | no: Deferred | homuncular functionalism |
| Brooks, "Intelligence without representation" (1991) | [LIT-436](../../record/literature.d/LIT-436.md), [NOTE-351](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-351.md) | in full | decomposition, built and run |
| List & Pettit, *Group Agency* (2011) | [LIT-391](../../record/literature.d/LIT-391.md) | no: Deferred | group agency |
| Huebner, *Macrocognition* (2013) | [LIT-426](../../record/literature.d/LIT-426.md) | no: Deferred | collective minds |
| Oizumi, Albantakis & Tononi, IIT 3.0 (2014) | [LIT-445](../../record/literature.d/LIT-445.md), [NOTE-365](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-365.md) | in full | the exclusion postulate |
| Kammerer, reply to Schwitzgebel (2015) | [LIT-409](../../record/literature.d/LIT-409.md), [NOTE-362](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-362.md) | in full | a functional anti-nesting principle |
| List, "What is it like to be a group agent?" (2016) | [LIT-401](../../record/literature.d/LIT-401.md), [NOTE-340](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-340.md) | in full | group agency yes, group experience no |
| Levin, "The computational boundary of a 'self'" (2019) | [LIT-439](../../record/literature.d/LIT-439.md), [NOTE-341](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-341.md) | in full | nested selves at every scale |

**The bridge, as the readings support it.** Agency is granted in both
directions, by Block, List and Levin. The dispute is over experience. Every
way to accept Minsky's downward move while refusing Schwitzgebel's upward
one takes one of two routes:

- an anti-nesting principle, stipulated by Putnam, postulated by IIT, or
  weakly justified by Kammerer;
- an architectural criterion, which would have to spare a loosely coupled
  society of mind while excluding a nation.

Nobody here computes that difference. [THEORY-043](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md) is `Proposed`, and its
`promote_when` names the criterion that would settle it.

**Corrections to [NOTE-131](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-131.md) the readings found**, held in the readings and
not yet applied to [NOTE-131](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-131.md) itself:

- Block's counterexample to Putnam is elementary-particle people, not tiny
  people as neurons.
- Schwitzgebel's Putnam "quotation" is a paraphrase, and the first
  appearance is 1967, from a 1965 colloquium.
- The "Brooks (1986)" of the group-mind tradition is D. H. M. Brooks, not
  Rodney Brooks.

Kammerer's reader also found that [NOTE-188](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-188.md)'s gloss of his principle omits
its second condition.

**Next on this seam, not filed:** Schwitzgebel's reply to Kammerer
(*Philosophia* 44, 2016) and D. H. M. Brooks, "Group minds" (1986). Reading
Huebner would most likely move the THEORY.

## What changed in the record's threads

- **[THEORY-043](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md)** (the bridge from Minsky to Schwitzgebel) gains a
  section from these readings:
  - Dennett's discharge of homunculi explains why the downward move is
    licensed for intelligence and the upward one is not.
  - Chalmers's organisational invariance narrows the dispute to
    architecture.
  - The combination-problem paper reaches the account's two routes
    independently.
  - Two new candidates for a principled line are named: Dennett &
    Kinsbourne against a conscious central part, and Chalmers 2019's
    "not mediated" condition. Neither yet meets `promote_when`.
  - Searle and "Quining Qualia" are recorded as refusing the framing.
- **[THEORY-023](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-023.md)** (AI consciousness) gains candidate evidence, not yet
  added to it:
  - Chalmers's LLM paper, a fifth prior: under 10% for current models, 25%
    or more within a decade;
  - footnote 26 of the meta-problem paper;
  - Turing's other-minds reply;
  - Searle's concession that behaviour licenses ascription until the
    program is known.

## Corrections the readings found

Each is held in the reading that found it; none is applied to the older
note it concerns.

- **Adams & Aizawa 2001 does not contain "coupling-constitution
  fallacy".** The phrase is from their later work; [NOTE-180](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-180.md) misattributes
  it.
- **Clark's 2005 quotation of the parity principle differs from [LIT-097](../../record/literature.d/LIT-097.md)'s
  text.**
- **Chalmers's fading-qualia paper misdates Block** (1980/1981; it is 1978).
  It also says Block finds group minds "bizarre", which Block's n. 19
  disclaims.
- **Levin's "Chalmers 2013" is *Panpsychism and Panprotopsychism*, not the
  combination paper.**
- **"Artificial Intelligence as Philosophy and as Psychology" appeared first
  in *Brainstorms* (1978), not in Ringle (1979).**

## Not filed, and next

- Chalmers, "Moving Forward on the Problem of Consciousness" (1997), his
  reply to Dennett.
- Dennett, "Darwin's 'strange inversion of reasoning'" (PNAS 2009), the
  readable source for "competence without comprehension".
- Dennett's 2007 joint review of *I Am a Strange Loop* and *The Emotion
  Machine*.
- Zuboff, "The Story of a Brain".

**Possible topic words, recorded and not added:** `computation` (what
implementation is) and `artificial-intelligence` (AI and robotics design),
with the earlier `knowledge-representation` and `cognitive-architecture`.

## How the record stood on the self

`identity` carried 39 works about three different things: the identity and
individuation of things (structural realism, quasi-sets, the Yoneda lemma),
biological individuality, and personal identity and the self. A reader
looking for the self met quasi-set theory first. No THEORY touched the
self, and the personal-identity literature the record's cognitive-science
and AI readings answer to was almost entirely missing: no Locke, Hume,
Parfit, Williams, Lewis, Olson, Schechtman, Strawson, Gallagher, Zahavi or
Metzinger.

## The vocabulary

- **`self-and-personhood`** ([ADR-015](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-015.md)) holds what a self or a person is and
  what makes one persist. Fifteen existing works took it, and every self
  filing above leads with it.
- **`identity` became `individuation`** ([ADR-015](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-015.md), at the owner's
  suggestion). With the self moved out, what was left was the
  individuation of things, and "identity" read alone invites the personal
  sense. The 41 bearers changed in place.
- **`phenomenology`** ([ADR-016](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-016.md)) is for the first-person description of
  experience as a method. A filing agent proposed it for Zahavi, and the
  owner accepted. Six works carry it, none first.

## For the next person

Three agents filed the self literature into one checkout at once, each
running only `luria new`. A `luria link --fix` run by the integrator spells
targets into their in-progress files too; that is harmless, since it only
spells links. Integrating each batch in a separate worktree at HEAD, with
`repair`, `link --fix`, `index` and `lint` run there, kept every commit
linted without waiting for the slowest agent.

## Social ontology

*2026-10-02 03:57:03 · curation · record*

The owner asked how the record covered social ontology, then for the
literature to be filed. The record held the philosophy of mind of groups
(Schwitzgebel's conscious United States, Kammerer, List, with List & Pettit
and Huebner unread) and almost nothing on what a group, an institution, a
convention or a social kind is. Searle appeared only for the Chinese Room.
`social-ontology` was added first ([ADR-017](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-017.md)) and six existing works took
it; then three agents filed 24 works in parallel. Eight were read in full.

This is the thinnest part of the batch. Searle's 2006 paper is his own
restatement of the 1995 theory, and Bratman's précis states his
reductive view and sets it against "Margaret Gilbert and John Searle", so
two of the three positions are on record in their authors' words.
Gilbert's and Tuomela's are known only second-hand. A copy of "Walking
Together" exists behind a bot check and a Wayback snapshot the proxy
could not reach; it is the cheapest of these to turn into a reading.

relate.

## What it did to the record

[THEORY-043](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md) v3 takes a scoping note from Ritchie and Epstein: groups with
the same members can be distinct, only organised groups are concrete
wholes, and a group's facts may depend on non-members. So any criterion
for group minds has to say which group it is applied to. None of these
readings discusses group experience, so the account itself does not move.

The filing agent for Haslanger and Ásta noted that nothing in the
vocabulary names gender, race or feminist philosophy, and proposed
`feminist-philosophy`. Two works do not make a topic. It is left for a
filing that brings more.

## For the next person

The three agents cited one another's temporary codes, so the batches
could not be committed independently; the first two turned out to be
closed under citation and went in together. The lint caught five
`inactive-ok-file` lines vouching for codes their files only named in
places the lint does not count as citing; those lines were removed.
Agents writing directives without running the lint will keep doing this,
which is what the rule against writing them from memory is for.
